findings.message: This change adds personal data that the retention and erasure rules never reach. (1) `time.entry.deleted_by` (migration 0003) holds the acting person's id, but it is in neither `subject` nor `fields` of the `time.entry` entry. The old blocker lesson was about `time.entry.logged_by`; this is the same class of defect. (2) `time.change_request.before` and `.proposed` are jsonb copies of the entry's free-text `note`. They are not in the change-request entry's `fields`, so anonymising leaves the note text in place. Fix: add `deleted_by` to the time.entry rule's `subject` and `fields`, and add `before` and `proposed` to the change_request rule's `fields`. Also extend check-module-standard so it also flags `*_by` columns added by `alter table` and jsonb columns that copy personal columns.
findings.scenario: A PM deletes Tharushi's entry; later the PM files an erasure request. time.entry.deleted_by still holds the PM's id, because the request never matches that column. Separately, Tharushi files an erasure request after a change request. change_request.before.note ('Dentist appointment') survives the anonymise.

findings.message: The new 'Continue as …' link renders `href={to}`. `to` only checks that `next` starts with '/' and not with '//', so `/\evil.example` passes, and browsers treat a backslash as a slash. Before this change, `to` was only passed to Auth.js `redirectTo`, which validates it against the base URL; this raw anchor has no such check. Fix: resolve `to` with `new URL(next, origin)` and keep it only when the origin matches, or reject any backslash.
findings.scenario: A signed-in user opens /signin?next=%2F%5Cevil.example and clicks 'Continue as Tharushi'. The browser navigates to https://evil.example.

findings.message: credentialsSignIn revokes the browser's current session before it checks the new credentials. A failed sign-in therefore still ends a live session. Fix: sign in first, then revoke the session it replaced, for example in the Auth.js signIn callback or by comparing session stamps after success.
findings.scenario: Tab A shows the sign-in form from while the browser was signed out. Tab B then signs in as Maya. Tab A submits a wrong password: Maya's session is revoked and the AuthError redirect shows 'wrong password', so Maya is silently signed out in tab B.

findings.message: There are now two delete paths for an entry. `writeDelete` soft-deletes (sets `deleted_at` and `deleted_by`, and keeps the row, as the README says). The commit-draft `undo` still runs a hard `delete from time.entry`. The hard delete loses the row the README promises to keep, and it fails on the new `time.change_request.entry_id` foreign key whenever any request, open or closed, references the entry. Fix: make undo call `writeDelete` (or the same soft-delete SQL) and reuse its event.
findings.scenario: A commit draft is accepted, then the week is submitted. The owner calls request_time_change and the request is declined. The approver sends the week back and the person undoes the suggestion. The undo fails with 'violates foreign key constraint change_request_entry_id_fkey'.

findings.message: The fix that makes the confirm card match the stored entry (`checkCard`, hoursBefore) runs only when the card is proposed. correctEntry and deleteEntry do not re-check when the write runs. The change-request path pins `revision` and refuses a moved entry, but these two tools don't. Fix: put `hoursBefore` (or the revision read at propose time) into the input and refuse the write in the service when the locked entry no longer matches.
findings.scenario: Tharushi gets a card reading 'Hours 10 h → 6 h'. Before she confirms, a PM corrects the entry to 8 h with a reason. Tharushi confirms and the entry becomes 6 h, overwriting the PM's fix without warning, while the card she confirmed said 10 → 6.

findings.message: `requestRows` applies `limit 200` across the whole tenant before `listRequests` filters by viewer, status or week. Any request outside the 200 newest silently disappears, and the result looks complete. This affects get_change_requests, the Team time 'Change requests' card, MyRequests and the 'Review change requests' suggestion. Fix: push the viewer, status and week filters into SQL and apply the limit after them, or say plainly when the list was cut off.
findings.scenario: A tenant has 250 change requests, most of them applied or declined. Maya's one pending request is older than the newest 200. Team time shows no change-requests card, and get_change_requests returns [] for her.

findings.message: `reason(e)` puts the database driver's raw error message into each per-person result. That message reaches the done card, the model (the result is quoted to it) and the audit `after`. This is the raw-error leak that toolFailure and doneNote were fixed for, now on a new path. Fix: map known refusals (Error from decide/writeRemind) to their message, and replace anything else with a logged reference such as 'couldn't be done (ref …)'.
findings.scenario: An approval insert fails on a constraint. The card and the chat reply read 'Ayesha Rahman: failed (duplicate key value violates unique constraint "approval_week_id_key")', and that text is stored in core.audit_event.after.

findings.message: Pins of a single change request (`requestPin`: `get_change_requests` with `{ id }`) resolve through a tool declared `pin: "view"`. A record pin should come from a read tool with `pin: { id, of }`, so its label is read back from the record (059). Fix: give the tool an `{ id: "id", of }` spec that returns the request's label, or add a dedicated `get_change_request` read tool.
findings.scenario: Pin a change request, then rename the person. The reopened chat keeps the stale label '<old name>, change request', because a view pin is never relabelled from the record.

findings.message: The published contract changed: `EntryLogged.revision` is now required, and there are new event types and payloads. The README still says 'Version 1' with no version note, and contracts.test.ts covers none of the new payloads (EntryCorrected, EntryDeleted, Change*). Bump the version, note it in the README and add the payload contract tests.

The session-gone `alertdialog` has `aria-modal`, but it doesn't trap focus or mark the rest of the page `inert`. Keyboard users can tab to the controls behind it, which goes against the WCAG and keyboard-complete commitment and against the dialog's own text ('this tab can't send or confirm anything'). Fix: set `inert` on the app root while the dialog is shown, or render it in a modal `<dialog>`.

Docs and code disagree. The 070 mock section still shows a per-row '✦ Fix these hours' button, but amendment 4 and the README say rows carry only pins, with no Fix buttons. The new block is also headed '068 Overview deltas' although it holds sections 073, 072, 071, 070, 069 and 068. Update the mock in its own change, and fix the comment.

Applying a change request that moves an entry to another project skips the project-scope check that correct_time_entry runs (`fixedBy` → `mayFix(v, owner, newProjectId)`). The `whoFor` callback here only looks up names. So an approver who is in the week's chain through project A can move the owner's hours onto project B, which they don't approve. Fix: in `whoFor`, check `mayFix(viewerOf(ctx), entry.user_id, projectId)` (or reuse `fixedBy`). Do the same check in `proposeDecide`/`checked`, so chat shows no card for a move the approver can't make. Add a variant test: a move to a managed project, to an unmanaged project, and with no move.
findings.scenario: Kasun asks to move his Fleet Tracker entry to HR Insights. Nimal (PM of Fleet Tracker only) runs decide_change_request apply. Expected: refused. Actual: the entry now sits on HR Insights, a project Nimal has no approve scope for.

findings.message: AC-52 (ending the browser's earlier session on a switch) runs only in `credentialsSignIn`. The Microsoft/OIDC provider form calls `signIn` directly, so a sign-in through Entra from a sign-in tab that was already open leaves the replaced session row unrevoked. Fix: run the same `sessionStamp` + `endSwitchedSession` step in the provider action, or in the Auth.js signIn callback so every provider gets it.
findings.scenario: Tab A shows /signin while signed out. Tab B signs in as Kasun. In tab A the person clicks 'Sign in with Microsoft' and signs in as Maya. Kasun's auth.session row keeps revoked_at null and is never audited as switched.

findings.message: `usable` turns a `when` check that throws (for example a DB read failure) into 'not offered'. A broken check looks the same as 'nothing to do here', and nothing is logged. Log the failure, so an outage is visible.
findings.scenario: teamWeek fails because the DB is down. Approvers see no 'Approve submitted timesheets' suggestion and no error anywhere.

findings.message: The change-request pin names one record by id, but it resolves through get_change_requests, which declares `pin: "view"`. Under 059, a record pin needs a read tool with `pin: { id, of }`. Give the tool (or a single-request read tool) a record pin spec.

This change's mock section still shows per-row '✦ Fix these hours' buttons, which contradicts amendment 4 (rows carry pins and no Fix buttons). The diff also adds mock sections owned by other changes (066, 068, 069, 071–073) under a '068 Overview deltas' comment. The module standard says the mock is read-only during a build.
